YouTube on CarPlay No More: Popular App APTV No Longer Working After iOS 27.2
18 photos
Photo: Florin Profir/autoevolution
YouTube isn’t officially supported on Android Auto and CarPlay (not yet, at least), but unofficially, users have been able to access Google’s video platform for quite some time. One of the apps that made this possible on CarPlay has stopped working recently, and the developer says Apple’s latest iPhone update is the one to blame.
APTV is an app whose main selling point is controversial, to say the least. The application allows users to watch YouTube through a browser, essentially unlocking the functionality that Apple has until now kept locked.
The iPhone maker paved the way for video apps on CarPlay with the release of iOS 26.4, but so far, video app support still hasn’t reached the point where users can install YouTube and start watching videos in their cars.
This is why APTV has become so popular. With a plug-and-play approach, APTV allowed users to install the app from the App Store, point the browser to YouTube, and load a video. It was that easy, and the app even offered additional functionality like logging in with a Google account.
The most controversial part was the video watching capabilities while the car was in motion. Users have reported a mixed experience on this front, and while some said that APTV did not allow them to watch the videos when they started driving, others claimed that the playback continued. This mixed experience could also be linked to the CarPlay head unit, as a factory-installed system is more likely to prompt a block when motion is detected.
Apple shipped iOS 27.2 this week, and it turns out that APTV stopped working altogether. The reason, the app developers say, is that the update has disabled this functionality on iPhones.
“Apple has disabled this CarPlay video functionality in iOS 27.2, so this is not an issue that we can fix through an APTV software update,” the developers told an app user. The only fix, they claim, is downgrading an iPhone to the previous iOS version.
The reason invoked by the APTV team doesn’t provide more context, but it looks like the “disabled functionality” that the devs highlight is actually a streaming video vulnerability that Apple has patched in iOS 27.2. I have reached out to both companies for additional information and will update the article if and when I hear back.
Video apps are still coming to Android Auto and CarPlay, and right now, it looks like Google users are more likely to get their hands on these apps first. Google has already announced support for video apps in the spring of this year, with the Cielo update for Android Auto expected to go live later this year or in the first quarter of 2027.
When this new app category is unlocked on Android Auto, users will be allowed to watch videos when their cars are stationary. An audio-only mode will be available in apps that support it, thereby blocking video when cars start moving.
